For Appellants : Mr. P.K.Tulsyan, Advocate For Respondent No.3 : Mr. N.K.Malaviya, Advocate
(Single Bench) Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay K. Agrawal Judgment on Board 06.04.2026
1.

The appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 seeking enhancement of the amount under award dated 10.10.2018 passed by the learned
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kondagaon in Claim Case No.54/2018.

2. Mr. P.K.Tulsyan, learned counsel for the appellants, would submit that the contributory
negligence has not been established and no witness has been examined by the insurance company
and furthermore, on the other heads also, less amount of compensation has been awarded.

Therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed and the amount of compensation be enhanced suitably.
3.
Mr. N.K.Malaviya, learned counsel for the insurance company/ respondent No.3, would support the impugned award and submit that the appeal preferred by the claimants is liable to be dismissed.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions made herein-above and gone through the records meticulously.

5. So far as the contributory negligence is concerned, though the insurance company has taken a plea that the stationery vehicle was dashed by the deceased, but in this behalf no evidence has been adduced.

Furthermore, as per the statement of eye-witness Sulo (AW-2), the stationery vehicle/offending vehicle didn't have the reflectors on, therefore, the plea of contributory negligence is not established and, as such, the appellants are entitled for full compensation.
6.

Learned Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased Dhanraj Netam to be Rs. 4,500/-
per month, however, in the opinion of this Court, as per the Chhattisgarh Minimum Wages Notification issued by the office of Labour Commissioner, Chhattisgarh, the monthly income of the deceased ought to have been taken as Rs. 7,930/- per month.

Accordingly, this Court is computing the compensation as below:-
Heads
Compensation
awarded
Compensation awarded by the Tribunal by this Court Income as per Rs. 4,500/- per month = Rs. 7,930 per month = minimum wages Rs.

54,000/- per annum Rs. 95,160/- per annum Add future Rs. 54,000 + 21,600 = Rs.
95,160 + 38,064 = prospects @40% Rs. 75,600/- = Rs. 1,33,224/- Deduction of 1/3 Smt. Manti Netam vs Chandakaramu Naidu on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68624726/
2
Multiplier of 17 Rs. 50,400 x 17 = Rs. 88,816 x 17
Contributory 50% = Rs. 4,28,400/-

Nil  Negligence  Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/- Rs. 18,000/-
 Funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000/- Rs. 18,000/-
 Love & affection Rs. 40,000/- Rs. 1,32,000/-
 (spousal, filial &
 (44,000 x 3)
 parental  consortium)

In view of the aforesaid analysis, the amount of compensation of Rs. 4,98,400/-
awarded by the Claims Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.
16,77,872/-.
Hence, after deducting the amount of Rs. 4,98,400/-, the claimants are entitled for an additional amount of Rs. 11,79,472/-.
The concerned respondent is directed to deposit the amount of compensation as enhanced by this Court within a period of 45 days.
The additional amount of compensation shall carry interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of claim application before the Tribunal till its realization.
Rest of the conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
8. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent as indicated herein-above.
